maya: Heads-up — new reranker (rnk-v3-ptq) looks fine on overall NDCG but MRR drops ~4-6% on short-snippet queries where docs contain multiple sentence breaks. Small repro attached below.
liam: Can you paste a minimal example from the holdout that shows the delta?
sarai: FWIW we saw similar short-snippet sensitivity on an older 4-bit run, might be a tokenization/prefix issue.
maya: Minimal pair:
```
query: "how to set CORS headers for S3 static site"
docA: "Use bucket policy.\nMake sure to add CORS config in console.\nSee docs."  -> MRR rank 1

docB: "To set CORS, edit the S3 resource policy.\nThen configure via the CLI." -> becomes rank 2 after ptq
```
liam: Huh. Those linebreaks are 

explicit. Could PTQ have changed how embeddings/attention handles 
 tokens around newlines?
maya: That's my intuition. I ran a quick diff of tokenization fp16 vs int8 for docA: fp16 token stream contains explicit "\n" tokens, int8 seems to merge neighboring punctuation into same token causing shifted attention windows.
zane: Can you paste token ids?
maya: Short snippet: fp16 ids -> [101, 345, 12, 999, 102]; ptq ids -> [101, 345, 1299, 102] (the newline got folded into previous token).
julian: If newline folding changes KV-cache alignment, that could change reranker scores even if model weights are similar. We should test two things: 1) tokenizer parity check; 2) run ablation with/without sentence-boundary marker.
sarai: Agreed. Quick tests: add explicit <SENT> tokens at sentence breaks in preprocess and run 1k sample eval. If MRR recovers, it's a preproc workaround.
ops-bot: :robot_face: queued job eval-run-1768012345: ./eval --model rnk-v3-ptq --split short-snippets --preproc add_sentence_marker --samples 1000
liam: Also try running the same eval but with FP16 weights on the same hardware to rule out runtime kernel differences: ./eval --model rnk-v3-fp16 --split short-snippets --samples 1000
maya: Started both jobs. Initial glance: ptq with <SENT> gives +3% MRR vs ptq baseline, fp16 still slightly above ptq+marker by ~1%.
zane: That suggests a partial mitigation but not full parity. Could be quantized attention scaling mismatch. Can you dump attention norms for a failure case?
maya: Will dump for the top 5 mismatches. Quick log snippet:
```
case id 4231: fp16 score 0.87, ptq score 0.63
attention_norms_fp16: [0.12, 0.09, 0.30, ...]
attention_norms_ptq:  [0.11, 0.05, 0.18, ...]
```
julian: Looks like head 3 magnitude collapsed in ptq. Head-wise pruning/scale could explain it. We should check our PTQ recipe: was range calib per-layer or per-head?
sarai: It was per-tensor. Try per-channel (per-head) calibration sweep on a small batch to see if head-wise scales recover.
liam: Also file a short eval slice for doc formatting types: newline-heavy vs paragraph vs bullet-list. We need to quantify where the worst regressions are and ship holdout-goldens for regression tests.
maya: Agree. I'll create the slice and a small golden set of 500 items for CI.
ops-bot: :white_check_mark: job eval-run-1768012345 completed (2h). Results gist: ptq baseline MRR -5.1%, ptq+<SENT> -2.3%, fp16 -1.2% vs gold. Full results uploaded to: https://redwood.internal/rg/1768012345/results
zane: Next steps: 1) run per-head calib sweep, 2) try hybrid quant (attn int8, mlp int4), 3) add preprocessing normalization for sentence breaks in onboarding docs.
julian: I'll pick up the per-head calib PR. maya, can you add the golden slice + CI test?
maya: On it. Creating PR with dataset + small eval job that runs on model bringup. Will tag the PR with @julian and @sarai.
sarai: Nice. Also update the model onboarding checklist: add 'tokenizer parity check for whitespace/newline' under quantization section.
liam: Thanks all. If someone sees other failure modes (lists, code blocks) add them to the slice. :thumbsup:
maya: Closing loop once PR merges and we rerun baselines. Thanks!
